A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IDRBench, retaining its paper-triplet representation and three core tasks. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, support reliable comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of ten LLMs, including classification, recommendation, generated-text comparisons, and ranking-correlation analyses in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, human evaluations, an input-context ablation, negative-sampling validation, and fine-tuning results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The triplet representation, three core task procedures, and Swiss-tournament ranking remain. Appendix A.8 adds teacher-generated abstract rewrites and rationales followed by LoRA adaptation, introducing an auxiliary training procedure beyond v1's inference-based evaluation.

E1.justification: The three core tasks and six broad discipline categories remain, but v2 adds evaluation using 56 researchers' own publications across nine disciplines, full-paper inputs for I3, and SlimOrca instruction data for training. Conversely, v1's harder I2R scenario, with half the distractors drawn from the positive candidate's discipline, is removed.

E2.justification: The main comparisons remove o1-mini and Gemini-1.5-pro, replace Claude-3.7 with Claude-4, and add o4-mini, GPT-5-nano, Qwen-2.5, and Qwen-3. Additional comparisons include older Llama models and an untuned-versus-LoRA experiment. The retained Kendall analysis also drops comparators such as Llama-3.1 and DeepSeek-v3.

E3.justification: Positive triplets increase from 120 to 335, and collection extends from November 2024–January 2025 to November 2024–October 2025. Negative selection gains sub-discipline restrictions, and I3 Subset 2 changes from approximately 1:20 to 1:10 positives-to-negatives. Maximum output length changes from 500 to 1,500 tokens, and main classification reporting switches from F1 to Macro-F1. New human studies and fine-tuning introduce additional evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds a negative-pair audit, semantic-shortcut analysis, a 200-sample full-content ablation, TPR/TNR error analysis, alignment-motivated model comparisons, human studies, and fine-tuning evaluation. It removes v1's discipline-identification analysis and quantitative SciBERT/BLEU/ROUGE idea-quality comparison. The original qualitative example remains as Figure 14, while Kendall analysis survives in reduced form.

E5.justification: v2 introduces standard errors for human ratings in Figure 5 and Table 9, dispersion statistics for semantic similarities, and agreement and false-negative-rate estimates for the negative-pair audit. Wilcoxon testing is retained. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds for the main LLM evaluations.

E6.justification: The main result tables are replaced under changed data, metrics, and comparator membership, so their differences are not same-setting performance gains. For example, v1's two I2R levels are led by Gemini-1.5-pro at 0.703 and 0.662 MRR; v2's single setting is led by Qwen-2.5 at 0.661. New outcomes include a 5.8% estimated false-negative rate, human abstract-correctness ratings of 3.963/5, and I3 Subset 1 scores of 0.664 before versus 0.796 after LoRA fine-tuning.

T1.justification: The triplet notation and MRR equations are retained. Neither version supplies substantive theoretical results or proofs; v2's added creativity, sampling, and leakage arguments are conceptual or empirical rather than new formal derivations.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes that LLMs show IDR awareness but struggle to generate quality ideas. v2 instead claims that they generate valid, useful ideas verified by experts, while struggling to distinguish genuine interdisciplinary integration. It also introduces central claims about degraded performance from reasoning-oriented models and downstream uses of IDRBench.

C2.justification: v2 introduces explanations linking optimistic or conservative predictions to post-training targets and linking reasoning to reduced creativity. It adds interpretations concerning input-grounded integration, leakage, negative-label reliability, and semantic shortcuts. The limitations now discuss subjective, open-ended solution spaces, while the external user study acknowledges variable integration and interest ratings. v1's interpretation of low textual overlap as poor idea quality is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds augmentation prompts and teacher identity, human-evaluation instructions, an explicit dual-annotation acceptance rule, and LoRA settings including rank 32 and 218 training steps. It first specifies an I2R list length of 30 and replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Appendix A.8 alternates between 7B and 8B model names and leaves the held-out split insufficiently specified.

R1.justification: The original comparisons with SchNovel, IdeaBench, and ResearchBench remain, but v2 substantially extends its positioning into alignment and creativity research, citing West and Potts, Murthy et al., and Luyten and van der Schaar to support a new central interpretation. It also adds citation-based innovation and fine-tuning literature, while removing several works supporting v1's deleted overlap metrics.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset narrative, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The earlier detailed-analysis section is reorganized around error analysis and human evaluation, and prompts move into a dedicated late appendix section. The title, author information, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two columns. Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, and Figure 3's comparative bar chart becomes a discipline-network diagram. Separate main result tables are consolidated, and new error-rate charts, human-rating displays, training plots, and appendix tables are added. Existing annotation screenshots and the qualitative example are retained with altered placement and sizing.

improvement.justification: The negative-pair audit and direct human evaluations provide better evidence about label reliability and perceived usefulness than v1's unaudited sampling and overlap-based idea-quality assessment. These gains are limited by removal of the harder I2R scenario, uncontrolled attribution of model differences to alignment, and reporting inconsistencies. For example, Section 5.1 describes I2R scores as approximately 0.670 although Table 2 spans 0.446–0.661, and Appendix A.8 inconsistently identifies the fine-tuned model. The revision therefore provides a bounded net improvement rather than an unqualified strengthening.
